THIS IS THE HALF THM-0108's SCOPE SAYS CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED AT THE SEAM, in its own words: 'nothing here establishes that any of them speaks its provider's protocol correctly, selects the right key, or reaches the endpoint a deployment intended.' The seam's re-verification catches a mismatched key for ANY backend; what it cannot do is establish that a backend asked the provider what key it has.

AN OWNERSHIP GAP, NOT AN EVIDENCE GAP: 14 controls in the AWS adapter, 39 in the GCP one, 9 in the PKCS#11 one, and no unit cited any of them. THREE UNITS, one per provider, because each module exists only under its own non-default feature and a plain cargo test --workspace compiles all three to ZERO tests.

THE CONSTRUCTION-TIME HALF IS THE POINT. An adapter that skipped it would advertise a public key it had not established and fail every request at the seam instead of at startup — a deployment that comes up and refuses everything, rather than one that refuses to come up. A destroyed GCP key version whose public key cannot be fetched must not produce a signer at all. And an endpoint refused at CONSTRUCTION rather than at use is the difference between a deployment that will not start and one that sends a credential-bearing request to an operator-supplied host before noticing; R9's only Critical lived in exactly that gap.

NO CUSTODY CLAIM, AND IN PARTICULAR NO FIPS-L3 CLAIM. A Cloud KMS EC_SIGN_ED25519 key version may be SOFTWARE- or HSM-protected, and getPublicKey/asymmetricSign cannot establish which; the adapters are honestly labelled software-protection custody. Real FIPS-L3 custody evidence remains a DEFERRED obligation awaiting validated hardware, and is not weakened here to manufacture closure. Not a protocol-conformance claim either: each adapter's controls run against fixtures, and the live-infra lane is separate and off the merge path.
